subtitle: UNIFIED REAL MAPS — RETIRED LEGACY CHARTS, COMPATIBLE ROUTES, MISSIONS & WAYPOINTS
changes: Deprecated the multiple legacy illustrated Atlas maps without deleting saved missions, routes, bookmarks or personal waypoints; the real zone map is now the single primary map experience.

Added an in-page searchable directory of all 25 historic destination IDs, with direct real-map navigation for 7 supported legacy zones and an external map directory for locations not yet represented by an in-page sourced image.
Kept original mission planner and route library functional, added map handoff actions, and consolidated the manual coordinate editor into a collapsible advanced panel rather than a second blank map.
Personal pins now refresh immediately on the real zone map after a local save, import or delete; no changes to authentication, Cloudflare, backend or video vault.

Product correction based on owner feedback: the World Atlas now OPENS with a real game-derived zone map and immediate clickable points of interest, not the older decorative continent art or a blank coordinate editor. No player setup, character linking or multiple planner screens needed.

Added a focused, first-screen map interface with ten Retail zone maps, including current Midnight Zul'Aman (2437), Harandar (2413) and Voidstorm (2405) as the default/first choices. Their actual game-derived map images and selected POIs/flight nodes were verified on the external source. Previously supported Khaz Algar and Dragon Isles maps remain available, with direct provider links, attribution and a full-source fallback when image hosting is unavailable.

Curated directly actionable source-backed location samples, including current Midnight flight routes, portals, delves, quest hubs, plus known dungeons and raid points in older zones. Every pin exposes in-game X/Y and UI Map ID, with source links; these samples are not exhaustive nor actual player tracking.

Search and filter a zone's visible locations; click a marker or list item to see coordinates and source, copy an in-game waypoint macro, zoom with +/− and drag the enlarged image on desktop/mobile. The interface is built for immediate use rather than additional forms or click-through steps.

Existing manually saved v22 zone-coordinate pins appear automatically on the real zone images, separately marked Personal. The original pin editor, v16 mission goals, v18.1 route archive, illustrated v18.2 research Atlas and v22 Living Intelligence Director are preserved below as optional advanced tools.

Updated Command Center navigation and native search, the PROXIMUS Gateway card and user-facing Atlas descriptions so outdated art is no longer promoted as the primary map. No new browser storage keys, Blizzard APIs, OAuth permissions, video access or worker changes.

Dedicated structural/provenance and synthetic desktop Chromium/iPhone WebKit browser tests check direct visible source maps, click-to-select reference markers, search, zoom, saved coordinate overlays, remote media failure fallback and original user record preservation. External provider uptime and real mobile device verification remain separately pending.

Added a coordinate-aware World Atlas v22 laboratory: players can enter exact 0–100 zone-map X/Y positions tied to an in-game UI Map ID, choose a pin type, add personal descriptions and view clickable markers on a neutral coordinate grid or an optional user-owned, local-only zone map preview.

Referenced seven independently researched in-game UI Map IDs for selected Dragon Isles and Khaz Algar areas; invalid IDs and out-of-range coordinates are rejected. The existing illustrated continent map remains clearly labeled schematic, never falsely claimed to be a precise Blizzard map. User-provided coordinate records are sourced as manual.

Added one-tap copyable World of Warcraft in-game user-waypoint macros using C_Map.CanSetUserWaypointOnMap and UiMapPoint.CreateFromCoordinates, plus safe portable export/import of user waypoint JSON and immediate links to the user's original Atlas missions and adventure plans.

Integrated those optional published-equipment research snapshots into Character Nexus and the new Director as time-labeled source-backed evidence, never as automatic game inventory, ownership, or proof of equipment still being worn. Does not store OAuth tokens, full API profile payloads or any secret.
